clue.text: Most attractive, thanks to a top man

parts.note: TA is the informal British word for thanks
the king is the top man of a realm

explanation.surface: Someone at their most charming thanks a person at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: TAKING means charming or very attractive, and the setter stretches it to the superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taking is captivating or charming, highly appealing to look at.

clue.text: Judges seem set to make changes

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are told to change their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Judges appear ready to bring in reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make changes' rearranges SEEMSET into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem is to regard or rate, so one who judges something worthy esteems it.

clue.text: Within the home no-one backs increasing living-costs

parts.note: within means in
a flat is a home

indicators.note: backs says the words no-one are turned round, read from the end

parts.note: NO plus I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Nobody at home supports the rising cost of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns NO + I into ION, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists call a general rise in prices the rate at which living costs climb.

clue.text: Teutonic music writer

definitions.meaning: Teutonic describes the people of Germany
Sir Edward ... was an English composer of light opera

explanation.surface: A Teutonic composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward German (1862-1936) wrote the comic opera Merrie England.
explanation.definitionFit: Teutonic is a synonym for Germanic, and Edward German is a composer, a writer of music.

clue.text: A plant that's easy to grow?

definitions.text: A plant that's easy to grow?

parts.words: A plant that's easy to grow?
parts.note: an old name for a medicinal herb, and a plant that is easy to grow is uncomplicated

explanation.surface: A gardener asks for a low-maintenance plant.
explanation.walkthrough: In old herbalism a 'simple' is a medicinal plant; the question mark flags the second sense, easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicinal herb was called a simple, and the word also means easy or uncomplicated.

clue.text: Weller's dog

parts.note: something that wells up is a spring, and a breed of spaniel bears a matching name

explanation.surface: The dog belonging to a man called Weller.
explanation.walkthrough: Weller looks like a surname; read it as one that wells up, as water from a spring does, and the dog is a springer spaniel.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is a gundog breed of spaniel, and a spring is water that wells up.

clue.text: Fruit gives a guy energy

parts.note: a guy is a man
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Fruit gives a fellow some energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: For example, tell stories about males: subjects

indicators.note: about puts the words tell stories around the abbreviation for example

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
males are men

explanation.surface: Lying about men, for instance, to one's subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you 'tell stories' wraps around the abbreviation, giving LIEGE before the males follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudal vassals owed loyalty to their lord, being his subjects.

clue.text: He wouldn't appear personally, but sent in a worker

indicators.note: in places the word sent inside the insect word

parts.note: a worker is a bee, the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone who stayed away sent a worker along in their place.
explanation.walkthrough: The bee is the crossword's standard worker; 'in' tells you the word sent goes inside it, giving BSENTEE after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: One who is absent does not turn up in person.

clue.text: Garden re-designed by English aristocrat

indicators.note: the letters of garden are designed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman's garden is remodelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-designed' rearranges GARDEN to GRANDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank.

clue.text: Thought Latin best

parts.note: a thought is an idea

explanation.surface: A thinker considers Latin the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal is the perfect or finest possible example.

clue.text: A company-one a large number left

parts.note: a band is a company of people
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: One firm, one big crowd that departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abandoned has been deserted, walked away from.

clue.text: Request the second grade say

parts.note: B is the second grade after A
say signals an example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Ask for the second-best mark, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask humbly or plead is to make a request.

clue.text: Men get so excited finding something of much value

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Men are thrilled when they find a valuable jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges MENGETSO.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious stone such as a diamond is a valuable treasure.

clue.text: Oriental flower festival

parts.note: oriental means ..., abbreviated E
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: An Eastern flower show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' tempts as a river (something that flows), but here it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast of the Resurrection is held each spring.

clue.text: Getting busy early out for a duck!

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting up early and busy to go duck-hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BUSYEARLY. The Aylesbury is a white English breed of domestic duck, named after the Buckinghamshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aylesbury is a breed of domestic duck raised for meat.

clue.text: Repartee is good only in one's youth

parts.words: is good only in one's youth
parts.note: something good only when young is no good when old

explanation.surface: Witty banter suits only the young.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BAD IN AGE: what is good only in youth is bad in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful teasing talk, a witty exchange of remarks.

clue.text: A gold-plated blade

indicators.note: plated means covered, so the gold letters surround the A

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A sword with a gilded blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plated' puts A inside OR, gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of an oar is its blade, and a rower's oar is often called a blade.

clue.text: A non-drinker pains associates

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker
pains are aches

explanation.surface: A teetotaller hurts his companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Attachés are junior colleagues attached to an embassy, diplomatic associates.

clue.text: The woman who was a prison reformer and cook

definitions.text: The woman who was a prison reformer
definitions.meaning: Elizabeth ..., the Quaker who reformed English prisons
to cook in a pan with fat

explanation.surface: A woman who reformed prisons and also cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth Fry (1780-1845) campaigned to improve conditions in British prisons and appeared on the five-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Fry was the famous prison reformer, and to fry is to cook in hot fat.

clue.text: A relation not being heartless, will make a gift

parts.note: a relation is a telling, a tale

indicators.note: being heartless means the word not loses its middle letter

explanation.surface: A relative without a heart still has a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being heartless' removes O from NOT to give NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural gift or aptitude.

clue.text: Some manage badly and worry

indicators.note: some means only part of the word manage is used

explanation.surface: Some people manage poorly and fret.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag is to pester or harass someone persistently.

clue.text: A quiet place where serving men entertain

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, men serving in the army
to entertain someone is to treat them

explanation.surface: A peaceful spot where soldiers host guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a secluded refuge for rest.

clue.text: There's a supporter here and there quite out of control

indicators.note: out of control letters run wild and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Wild fans run riot here and there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite out of control' rearranges ANDTHERE. 'There's' and 'here' are link padding in this old clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower who sticks to a cause.

clue.text: Dredge the river and shut up!

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to pen is to shut up an animal

explanation.surface: Someone is told to dredge the river and be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging a channel makes it deeper.

clue.text: Tried, though it's stated otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise says the letters of stated are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Something tested, though it was claimed otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges STATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to try or sample it.

clue.text: A former copper is offensive but let off

parts.note: D is the old British penny, a copper coin before decimal currency
an offensive is a charge, an attack

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman is aggressive yet released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the old penny, D, from Britain's pre-1971 currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a gun is to fire it; to discharge a prisoner is to free them.

clue.text: Many blame the box

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
to rate is an old word for scold or blame

explanation.surface: Lots of people blame the box.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a wooden packing case.

clue.text: The poet maybe smokes

definitions.meaning: smokes in the sense of being on fire

explanation.surface: A poet who smokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns is the poet, and something that smokes is alight and on fire.

clue.text: This has a bad effect on the listeners

definitions.text: This has a bad effect on the listeners

parts.words: This has a bad effect on the listeners
parts.note: listeners are ears, so the reading is a pain in the ears

explanation.surface: A performance that pains the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listeners' looks like an audience, but it means the ears themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain inside the ear is a condition of the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Iron cutback

definitions.meaning: to iron is to take out the creases

explanation.surface: An iron reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DE-CREASE: to iron something removes its creases.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing takes out creases, and a reduction in amount is a lessening.

clue.text: Touching note followed by a letter causing a break

parts.note: re means touching or concerning
C is a musical note
ess is the spelt name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A note about a letter causes an interruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a pause or break in proceedings, as of Parliament.
